title: Tim Fulton (Small Business Matters · Vistage Chair Emeritus) — 'Don't wait until your business is successful to figure out how you want it to behave'
summary: Tim Fulton, president of the Atlanta-based advisory Small Business Matters and a Vistage Chair Emeritus, recommends the book to every small business owner. His firm also published a full review (bylined Kelly White), which works through financial gravity and the Costco, Patagonia and FedMart cases, and lands on the same point: good intentions aren't enough, the organisation itself has to be designed to resist the pull.
blockquote:
Don’t wait until your business is successful to figure out how you want it to behave. 

That’s one of the key messages from "Incorruptible" by Eric Ries. This thought-provoking book examines the relationship between purpose, profitability, culture, and long-term business success. It’s particularly useful for business owners who aren’t simply trying to build a more profitable company, but are trying to build a company that will still be worth being proud of 10 or 20 years from now.

I highly recommend this book for every small business owner.

source_urls.label: Full review on Small Business Matters — 'Ries believes this drift is not inevitable—but preventing it requires deliberate choices about incentives, measurements, culture, ownership, and governance.'
